aliases.name: Eater of Hearts
aliases.meaning: epithet from Book of the Dead

description.summary: An ancient Egyptian funerary demon depicted with the head of a crocodile, the foreparts of a lion, and the hindparts of a hippopotamus, who devours the hearts of the unworthy dead in the Hall of Two Truths.
description.full: Ammit (also Ammut, Ahemait) is a hybrid demon-figure of ancient Egyptian funerary religion. Her name is conventionally translated 'Devourer of the Dead' or 'Swallower of the Dead'. She is depicted with the head of a crocodile, the forequarters of a lion (or leopard), and the hindquarters of a hippopotamus — a composite of three of the most dangerous animals known to the Egyptian Nile world. Ammit's role is set in Chapter 125 of the Book of the Dead: in the Hall of Two Truths (the judgment of Osiris) the heart of the deceased is weighed on a scale against the feather of Maat. If the heart proves heavier than truth, Ammit consumes it — annihilating the deceased's existence and denying them the afterlife in the Field of Reeds (Aaru). Ammit was not worshipped, received no temples, and had no priesthood; rather, she was a feared guardian whose presence in tomb and papyrus imagery enforced the moral logic of the judgment. She becomes prominent in funerary iconography from the New Kingdom (especially the 19th Dynasty onward) and is shown beside the scales in such famous papyri as the Papyrus of Ani and the Papyrus of Hunefer.

etymology.origin: Ancient Egyptian, with the verb ʿm 'to swallow / devour' and the participle 'mwt 'the dead'.
etymology.meaning: 'Devourer of the Dead' or 'She who swallows the dead'.
etymology.first_use: Attested in funerary literature of the New Kingdom (c. 1550–1070 BCE), most prominently in the Book of the Dead.

related_phenomena.name: Anubis
related_phenomena.description: Conducts the weighing of the heart at which Ammit is present

related_phenomena.name: Osiris
related_phenomena.description: Presides over the judgment of the dead

related_phenomena.name: Maat
related_phenomena.description: Goddess of truth whose feather is weighed against the heart

related_phenomena.name: Taweret
related_phenomena.description: Hippopotamus-headed Egyptian protective demoness; iconographic relative

features.description: The head and jaws of a Nile crocodile
The forelegs and chest of a lion (or, in some depictions, a leopard)
The hindquarters and rear legs of a hippopotamus

physical.morphology: Tripartite composite hybrid, drawing each component from a top-tier predator or large dangerous animal of the Nile environment.

abilities.description: Consumes the heart of the deceased who fails the weighing against Maat's feather, annihilating their existence

range.description: Ammit appears in the funerary religion of ancient Egypt, with iconography distributed across tombs, papyri, and temples throughout the Nile Valley and the Egyptian-controlled regions of the New Kingdom.

first_recorded.source: Book of the Dead funerary literature

peak_activity_periods.description: Highest concentration of Ammit imagery in Theban funerary papyri

origins.cultural_roots: Ancient Egyptian funerary religion centred on the cult of Osiris and the moral judgment of the dead.
origins.earliest_accounts: Funerary literature of the New Kingdom, especially Chapter 125 ('Negative Confession') of the Book of the Dead.
origins.folklore_connections: Iconographically connected to the family of Egyptian protective and threatening hybrid demons (e.g. Taweret).

timeline.event: Earliest appearance of Ammit in New Kingdom funerary imagery
timeline.significance: Establishes the figure in the canonical judgment scene

timeline.event: Papyrus of Ani is produced (19th Dynasty); Ammit appears beside the scales in the judgment vignette
timeline.significance: Most famous individual Book of the Dead manuscript depicting Ammit

timeline.event: Papyrus of Hunefer (19th Dynasty) depicts the weighing of the heart with Ammit at the foot of the scales
timeline.significance: Classic visual reference for the Ammit motif

history.modern_era: Ammit is studied as part of Egyptian funerary religion and is widely recognised in popular culture, including the 2022 Marvel Studios series 'Moon Knight' in which Ammit features as a primary antagonist.

documentary.name: Papyrus of Ani
documentary.description: 19th Dynasty Book of the Dead papyrus depicting the weighing of the heart with Ammit beside the scales.

documentary.name: Papyrus of Hunefer
documentary.description: 19th Dynasty Book of the Dead papyrus with one of the best-known judgment vignettes featuring Ammit.

paranormal.name: Genuine afterlife agent
paranormal.description: In ancient Egyptian belief, Ammit was a real supernatural agent enforcing moral order in the afterlife.

skeptical.name: Symbolic personification of moral annihilation
skeptical.description: Egyptologists understand Ammit as a symbolic personification of the failed judgment — the annihilation of the unjust soul — rather than a worshipped deity.
evidence_cited: Absence of Ammit cult, priesthood, or temple
Iconographic role limited to judgment scenes

traditions: Egyptian Book of the Dead funerary tradition
stories: The judgment of the deceased before Osiris (Book of the Dead, Chapter 125)
folklore.beliefs: Ammit's threat enforced the moral logic of the negative confession; the dead asserted innocence of forty-two named transgressions before the gods.

film_tv: Moon Knight (Marvel Studios, 2022) — Ammit as principal antagonist
